summary: Neo Delay in Stereo mode with its filters open: the first track's Length (in its unit) becomes Sync and Feel, or a free Time; Feedback carries over to ±99 %; Dry thru and Wet out become a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Lengths count in Length unit: ticks (the default) are Buzz's whole samples per tick, so the echo follows the tempo; a length in ticks that is a note value (1 tick = 1/16 at 4 ticks a beat, 3 ticks = 1/8 dotted, 6 = 1/4 dotted …) becomes Neo Delay's Sync and Feel, which follow the tempo too; any other length, and lengths in ms or samples, a free Time at the song's tempo and rate.
Both in % of each echo fed back (Jeskola Delay's source: buf = in + fb · buf, (raw − 64)/64); Neo Delay's stops at ±99 %, where Jeskola's ±100 % never decays.
Jeskola Delay adds the dry signal (on or off) and its echoes at Wet out (raw/128); Neo Delay crossfades them and sets the output's level: mix = wet ÷ (dry + wet), output = dry + wet.

remarks: Jeskola Delay is mono: NeoBuzz Live gives it left + right summed (+6 dB for a centred sound) and it plays the same on both sides; Neo Delay in Stereo mode keeps the input's image, so a centred sound is the same and a panned one stays where it is. The +6 dB goes on the output connections, not the inputs: the line keeps the input's own level, under its saturator's knee (0 dBFS at Drive 0 dB), as Jeskola Delay's float line never saturates.

Each of Jeskola Delay's tracks is a tap of its own (up to 8); Neo Delay has one line a side: the first track's settings move, the others' are left out (their pattern columns write the same parameters, with a note).
Jeskola Delay's Max Delay attribute (1 s by default) caps its lengths; the mapping doesn't read attributes, so a longer length plays longer on Neo Delay (up to 5 s free, 10 s synced).

tolerance.measured: Windows, Neo Poly noise and chords into it, each side against its input: at its defaults (3 ticks, Feedback 50 %, Wet out 37.5 %, dry on) −0.0 dB, third octaves within 0.3 dB (chords −0.0 dB, within 0.5 dB); 120 ms, Feedback −60 %, wet only: −0.0 dB, within 0.4 dB. Its echoes, read from single bursts, are its source's: at 126 BPM a centred burst echoes on both sides every 357.1 ms (3 ticks, 15 750 samples) at −2.5, −8.5, −14.5 dB (Wet out × 2 for the summed input, then Feedback each pass), and at −50 % every other echo inverted; Neo Delay's land on the same samples
tolerance.why_not: Where the echoes build up, single third octaves move: 5 ticks (a free 595 ms), Feedback +80 %, Wet out 75 %: −0.1 dB on noise but 1.3 dB at 100 Hz, and on chords +0.2 dB but 2.2 dB at 400 Hz. Two probable causes, not separated: a free length lands on Time's step (0.085 %; 5 ticks, 26 250 samples, become 26 244), so each repeat lands 6 samples further from Jeskola's and the comb's teeth move against the chord's harmonics; and a long build-up reaches Neo Delay's saturator (its knee at 0 dBFS with Drive 0 dB), which Jeskola Delay's float line never has. Wet only at 120 ms, −60 % on chords: −0.4 dB, 1.1 dB at 630 Hz (the time exact, so probably the saturator on the chords' peaks). A panned input plays in the middle through Jeskola Delay (it is mono, dry and echoes) and where it is through Neo Delay; the comparison, with a centred sound, doesn't see that.
